# Effort.md stops telling readers Neo costs more to learn and set up

## Context

Tonight's release-blocking front-door pass reads every Benefits and README door with one question: where does a page undersell Neo, and where does it push the reader away? That pass runs through #20538, #20539, #20543 and #20519 (for #20518) under #20498.

I ran a phrase sweep at `dev` `b0e5fceb91` over the Benefits and Getting Started pages that none of those PRs touch. It found one push-away and two framework-shelf phrases. All other hits were neutral: "Stick with … when" pattern choices in the advanced guides, and "simple app" tutorial wording.

## The Problem

- `learn/benefits/body/Effort.md:13-14` opens the page's advantage with a cost: "While there might be a slightly higher initial learning curve or setup effort compared to starting with a trivial vanilla JavaScript website, this upfront investment is a strategic advantage."
  - The chart above it does start Neo's curve slightly higher, at "Web Site". But the curve crosses below vanilla JavaScript before "Simple Web Application", and below a typical framework before "Complex Web Application". So the page has an advantage to lead with.
  - The setup cost is one command. `npx neo-app@latest` sets up the workspace, the app shell and the dev server, then launches the app (`README.md` Quickstart).
- `Effort.md:17` repeats the cost: "This initial effort is quickly recouped".
- `Effort.md:19` ("a stark contrast to other frameworks") and `learn/benefits/body/Speed.md:7` ("most other JavaScript frameworks") put Neo on the framework shelf. `guide-authoring-bar.md:38` rules that out: "Never 'framework.'"

## The Architectural Reality

- The text and the chart are the operator's own: #6896, 2025-06-29, before coding agents wrote Neo's blueprints.
  - "Developers typically get up to speed within about a week" is his figure from experience, and it stays.
  - The chart stays as drawn, and the text stays consistent with it.
- A coding agent reads and writes Neo's JSON blueprints natively (`learn/benefits/body/JSONFirstUIs.md`). #20519 and #20545 now say so on the front doors, so this page should name it too.

## The Fix

- `Effort.md:13-20`:
  - Lead with where the curves cross, as the chart draws them.
  - State setup as one command.
  - Keep "within about a week".
  - Add that a coding agent reads and writes the blueprints natively, linking `JSONFirstUIs.md`.
  - Drop the "upfront investment" and "quickly recouped" framing.
  - Change "other frameworks" to "single-threaded libraries".
- `Speed.md:7`: change "most other JavaScript frameworks" to "most JavaScript libraries and frameworks".

Decision Record impact: none (docs only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The advantage section of `Effort.md` no longer opens with a cost.
  - It leads with where Neo's curve crosses below the others, matching the chart.
  - It names setup as one command (`npx neo-app`).
  - It keeps "within about a week".
  - It links `JSONFirstUIs.md` for agent fluency.
- [ ] AC-2: `git grep -n -i -E 'other (javascript )?frameworks' -- learn/benefits/body/Effort.md learn/benefits/body/Speed.md` returns nothing. Positive control: on `origin/dev` the same grep matches `Effort.md:19` and `Speed.md:7`.
- [ ] AC-3: `node ./buildScripts/util/check-relative-links.mjs` and `node ./buildScripts/util/check-whitespace.mjs` pass.

## Out of Scope

- The pages #20519, #20542, #20544 and #20545 change.
- The chart (`neomjs/pages`).
- "traditional frameworks" in `Effort.md:6` and `JSONFirstUIs.md`. Those lines describe other libraries without shelving Neo.
- The rest of `Effort.md`.

## Avoided Traps

- Claiming Neo costs nothing up front. The chart starts Neo's curve slightly higher at "Web Site", and the text must not contradict the picture above it.
- Deleting "within about a week": it is the operator's lived figure, not a cost claim.
- Inventing an agent-productivity figure: the page names the capability, never a number.
